name: MISSION0_LINE2
entries: Objective: Produce the most sophisticated latrine

name: MISSION0_LINE4
entries: As secretary of the European Science Foundation it is my privilege to invite you to participate in the 4th International Latrine Fair which will be held this time next year in Copenhagen.

name: MISSION0_LINE5
entries: It is my sincere hope that En-suite Privy Facilities will be our nascent millenniums transforming technology, in the same way that nuclear fusion was fifty years ago, and gunpowder was five hundred years ago.

name: MISSION0_LINE6
entries: As a participant in the fair you will have the opportunity to display your work to a panel of competitors, and observe the work of other companies active in the field.  A prize of $100,000 will be awarded for the best latrine, followed by two runner-up prizes of $20,000 each.

name: MISSION0_LINE7
entries: We look forward to seeing you in Copenhagen,

name: MISSION1_LINE4
entries: As a management consultant specialising in start-ups, you receive a message on your answering machine from the boss of a toilet manufacturer, who are struggling to push their goods out onto the market.  Can you bring their fortunes back to the watermark ?

name: MISSION1_LINE5
entries: §' My names Bendicks of U-Bendix and Flush.  You might not have heard of us but I bet youve sat on us once in a while.  You see, we do toilets.  Futuristic.  But the future aint bright.

name: MISSION1_LINE6
entries: Thats why were calling you.§The problem is - no-ones buying.  Theyre embarrassed to talk about the bright new future were offering.  Adjustable seats and  medical sampling.  I guess theyre happy to lock themselves in the dark ages of ball-cock and scale build-up.

name: MISSION1_LINE7
entries: I talked to HR and they say there aint no technicians or supervisors either, so productions running dry and they want top dollar for every effort they make. Well, I tried to talk to HR but were barely on speaking terms.

name: MISSION1_LINE8
entries: In fact, Im not getting on too well with R and D either: theyre not delivering the goods.  No patents, no royalties.  Hell, the atmosphere here just stinks!

name: MISSION1_LINE9
entries: Id give them a raise if they loosened up - or if I could afford it.  But weve hardly any stock left to float, and even if we do sell it, it wont bring us the royalties we need.  Hell, I dont know what went wrong !  You get the picture ?  I thought Id hand over to you before I threw in the towel.  I hope you cope with the strain better than I did. '

name: MISSION2_LINE2
entries: Objective: Reach a cash balance of 10.000.000$

name: MISSION2_LINE4
entries: So, you thought things were bad, well Im afraid theyre just about to get a lot worse.

name: MISSION2_LINE5
entries: Your little brother, who never was the brains of the family, has just had the bright idea of blowing his entire inheritance on a run down, formerly state-owned, loss-making roller blades factory in an unstable, Eastern bloc, ex-Soviet fledgling democracy.

name: MISSION2_LINE6
entries: As inflation grips the country, a demoralized and underskilled workforce, asking for little and contributing less, has watched their standard of living decline as their better-qualified counterparts move West. The privatization of the banking sector has left a financial gap only the mafia has rushed to fill.

name: MISSION2_LINE7
entries: And thats not the worst of it. The party may be over for the one-party state, but the vast unwieldy Gosudarstvenny Rollers Institut has until recently held a total monopoly on production and research.

name: MISSION2_LINE8
entries: Still heavily subsidized by the government, it is understandably unkeen to relinquish it. And its employees arent too quick to rock the boat either since, for all its faults, the factory still provides a degree of security far more attractive than your cynical brand of Western capitalism.

name: MISSION2_LINE9
entries: For the sake of the family honor, sort this mess out and make a crisp ten million on your brothers behalf. Then he can go and set up that Internet Start-up in Silicon Valley like you told him to.

name: MISSION3_LINE2
entries: Objective: Be the last surviving player

name: MISSION3_LINE4
entries: It is not a question of whether you are going to go bankrupt: yours is a lost cause.

name: MISSION3_LINE5
entries: Not only has hyperinflation sent prices spiraling out of control, but your investors, once so confident and generous, have embarked on a damage limitation exercise.

name: MISSION3_LINE6
entries: They are going to bleed you dry. You have to pay daily penalties which are constantly being raised.

name: MISSION3_LINE7
entries: To keep your dignity intact, you resolve to be the last company to pack up and go home, and hang on as long as possible.

name: MISSION4_LINE2
entries: Objective: To have the highest bottom line when the market crashes

name: MISSION4_LINE4
entries: The markets have been sky-high for too long. No-one but the most naïve think it can last forever: whoever heard of boom without bust?

name: MISSION4_LINE5
entries: Certainly this babys boom has been very impressive indeed, and all the signs are her bust is gonna be just as spectacular. Shes gonna crash, and soon.

name: MISSION4_LINE6
entries: Every two-bit analyst can tell you that. The problem is, when? And how much time is there left to cash in on what remains?

name: MISSION4_LINE7
entries: The winner in this game will be the one who has the most money when everything goes belly-up

name: MISSION5_LINE2
entries: Objective: Get out of the red by raising your bottom line up to 0

name: MISSION5_LINE4
entries: You have been sent to a start-up which is about to go down the tubes and deeply in debt. Your predecessors strategy was disastrous.

name: MISSION5_LINE5
entries: He invested everything in research. You have a state-of-the-art lab and have researched every technology.

name: MISSION5_LINE6
entries: You have expert researchers who are very expensive.

name: MISSION5_LINE8
entries: §The investors want results and are giving you a year to turn the place around.

name: MISSION6_LINE2
entries: Objective: Reach a cash balance of 2.500.000$

name: MISSION6_LINE4
entries: You havent been paying your backhanders to the Finance Ministry, so the government has carried out its threat: a product embargo. You cant sell anything.

name: MISSION6_LINE5
entries: To make things worse, your rival is taking this splendid opportunity to put you out of the picture for good.

name: MISSION6_LINE6
entries: §Nothing is beneath him: espionage and intimidation are part of your daily routine.

name: MISSION6_LINE7
entries: And dont count on the law to help you, because in this country, the lawyers are rotten to the core and none of them would work for you anyway.

name: MISSION6_LINE8
entries: §The only way to survive is to fill the occasional production and research orders you receive from foreign companies. Make as much money as you can, and get out while the goings good.

name: MISSION7_LINE2
entries: Objective: Reach a product rating of 60% by the emotives

name: MISSION7_LINE6
entries: Despite everything, you have decided to stay with your company and compete with the secret research labs who have all the resources they need.

name: MISSION7_LINE7
entries: You are convinced that youll find a market: its up to you to position yourself correctly and make a killing.

name: MISSION8_LINE2
entries: Objective: Be the last surviving player

name: MISSION8_LINE5
entries: §As you are quite the gentleman, you despise your rivals, who have joined forces to scupper your firm by fair means or foul, and they are mostly foul.

name: MISSION8_LINE6
entries: Not to stoop to their level, you decide to call on the services of the legal profession, and launch repeated court actions. The problem is finding the guilty party, because if you sue an innocent rival, you lose.

name: MISSION8_LINE7
entries: If you do nab the culprit, however, the fine will be so high he will be forced to throw his hand in. Hold out against the cowardly attacks of the competition and have them convicted one by one.
